rows.medi_said: Oh, is it, is it، is it عصافير؟
rows.why: Hunting for the word 'sky' he guessed عصافير (earlier 'عصا-' then 'that's bird') and she said no, that is birds; she gives سما at 16:35.
He said he forgot the word for sky and Amal supplied سما (sheet: sky | Sama | سما).
Engine wrote 'فئة واحدة؟', probably غيمة واحدة؟; after it he moves from غيم to the plural غيوم (16:51) and she says مم; sheet has غيمة only, so this may not be an error.

rows.medi_said: When, when do you look at the sky? When do you watch the sky?
rows.amal_said: No، امتى بتتطلع على الشمس would be when do you watch the sky؟ امتى الشمس بتطلع؟ ... When does the sun go up؟
rows.wrong: When do you watch the sky? (heard بتطلع as look at)
rows.right: امتى الشمس بتطلع (when does the sun go up)
rows.why: He repeated her sentence right but took بتطلع to mean 'look at'; she said No and explained, and he says 'I forget that you can use بتطلع as to go up' (18:18).

rows.amal_said: Or just حجر. Are stone. ... Made of is different than made.
rows.proposed_rule: To say something is made of a material, just name the material as the predicate (الشوارع حجر = the streets are stone); no 'were made with' (عملت مع حجر).
rows.why: He built English 'were made with stone' as عملت مع حجر; Amal gave the plain nominal sentence and said 'Made of is different than made'.
